report.summary: The one failure is a 5 s Page.goto timeout on /books, caused by a random server-side delay of 0 to 8 s in list_books (app/main.py:150), which the books page calls on every render. Treat it as flaky, not a product bug: the outcome depends on how long the random sleep runs. First step is to remove or make the delay deterministic in the app (or stub it for tests) so the UI test stops depending on chance.

causes.title: Books page render sleeps a random 0-8 s, exceeding the 5 s navigation timeout
causes.explanation: list_books() calls time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) before querying the database (app/main.py:149-150). render_books() calls list_books() on every /books render (app/main.py:256), so each page load takes a random 0-8 s. The test fixture sets the default Playwright timeout to 5000 ms (tests/ui/conftest.py:4-7), and page.goto waits for the 'load' event. Whenever the sampled delay exceeds about 5 s, goto times out. The same code can pass on a rerun, so this is flaky. The test is correct to expect the page to load, and the root cause is the app's random delay plus a tight timeout. Other UI tests that open /books (for example test_added_book_is_listed) are exposed to the same delay, so they may fail intermittently too. The failing test id is the only one in this run.
evidence: tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:23 BooksPage(logged_in_page).open() is the call that timed out, and the traceback points at tests\support\pages.py:34 self.page.goto("/books").
Error: "Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: navigating to \"http://127.0.0.1:53126/books\", waiting until \"load\"".
app/main.py:256: "books": list_books(user["id"]), inside render_books(), which serves GET /books.
tests/ui/conftest.py:4-7: autouse fail_fast fixture calls page.set_default_timeout(5000), with the docstring saying nothing should take longer than 5 s.

Only one test failed in this run and it is the only one that navigates straight to /books before any other step, which fits a per-run random delay, but the run does not show the sampled delay values, so this is inferred from the code rather than from timing logs.
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the time.sleep from list_books in app/main.py, or gate it behind an env flag that tests never set. If the latency is meant to be realistic, keep it deterministic and well under the timeout, or give page navigation in the UI tests an explicit larger timeout. Then rerun the UI suite several times to confirm it is stable.
